title: Watergate document shredding at Bendix and Saudi troop training

tellings.quote: When Watergate happened, I was working for Bendix at the time and um our whole division went absolutely nuts because of all the stuff we had on paper. So suddenly the the the shredders are operating overtime, right?

plain: When the Watergate scandal broke in the 1970s, the political break-in affair around President Nixon, the shredders at a company called Bendix ran overtime, according to the writer Peter Levenda, who is billed on the show as a CIA historian. Levenda says he worked for Bendix at the time and that his whole division "went absolutely nuts because of all the stuff we had on paper." The story is also tied to training troops in Saudi Arabia, though his quoted words are about the shredding, which suggests the company had papers it did not want found.
